audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Jax the 2+ items row while whys[6] and late both say a fed Warwick wins there, and both give level 6 to Skill while whys[4] says 'the all-in tilts my way'. The packet chart agrees with the text (Jax, Jax, Skill, Skill, Jax, Jax, Warwick), not the chart.
audit.why: At 6, Grandmaster's Might's resists tank his drain and Counter Strike's stun can interrupt Infinite Duress, which the kit marks as a channel. Late, Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on a 70s cooldown at rank 3 that Counter Strike cannot dodge, and Eternal Hunger triples its healing under 25%.
audit.corrected: Level 6 row set to Jax and the 2+ items row set to Warwick in both layers as one atomic group, with ratings and phases[6].why brought in line. Rows 0 and 2 left as they are: whys[0] calls level 1 a flat window for Jax and whys[2] gives level 3 to Jax on Counter Strike, and the prose is the better-argued source there.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json R cd 110/90/70, channel + hardCC flags, P text

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is written as "Grandmaster at Arms" in spikes[1].text, mid, late and wants.you[1].
audit.why: The ability is Grandmaster's Might, 110/100/90s — phases[4].why already uses the real name.
audit.corrected: Renamed in all four content strings. Warwick's spikes otherwise verified: Infinite Duress at 6 (110s at rank 1, 70s at rank 3) and the late window where Eternal Hunger's healing triples below 25% health.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned anywhere in this matchup — not in the level chart, the spikes, or the trading rules.
audit.why: It is the ability that most directly breaks Jax's pattern in the 4-5 window: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that blunts the Empower-Leap punish, then a 1-second flee on re-activation that walks you out of your own auto chain, all on a 15s cooldown at rank 1 versus Counter Strike's 17s. Its absence is why the mid-lane rows read as generic.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now names Primal Howl, its damage reduction window, the fear, and the 15s timer.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json E cd 15/14/13/12/11, hardCC flag, Riot text '2.5 seconds ... flee for 1 second'

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early is right: Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress all carry the heal flag, so three of his five abilities heal.

edits.after: Counter Strike online — dodge his auto-attacks then recast to stun, and with no pre-6 dash he eats the full Empower-Leap punish, the trade his kit walks straight into.

edits.before: Both ult. Grandmaster at Arms' Armor/MR burst lets you tank his Q-heal sustain DPS, but his R is a full suppress that holds you in place — and Counter Strike only dodges autos, not his R. Bait or save the stun to interrupt his R channel, or all-in only after he's used it.
edits.after: Both ult. Grandmaster's Might's Armor/MR burst lets you tank his Q-heal sustain DPS, but Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on 110s at rank 1 that Counter Strike cannot dodge — it dodges autos only. It is a channel, so save the stun to interrupt it, or all-in after he spends it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay close — I rank Counter Strike so the dodge-stun is up more often, but he ranks Q heal and Blood Hunt to stick on me, so neither of us runs away with it. At 6 it's all about his R: Grandmaster at Arms gives me the Armor/MR to tank his drain DPS, but his suppress is hard CC that E can't dodge, and it holds me in place for his whole combo. I never commit until I've forced his R out or saved the stun to interrupt his channel. Win the fight where his R is down; respect it where it's up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay close — you rank Counter Strike so the dodge-stun is up more often, but Primal Howl answers it: 2.5s of damage reduction, then a 1s fear that walks you out of your own punish, every 15s. At 6 it is all about his R: Grandmaster's Might gives the Armor/MR to tank his drain DPS, but the 1.5s suppress is hard CC that E cannot dodge and holds you there for his whole combo. It is a channel, so never commit until you have forced it out or kept the stun to interrupt it.

edits.before: Past first item my on-hit ramp from Grandmaster at Arms plus Trinity lets me out-DPS his Q heal in a clean side-lane 1v1, so this is where I press the split and force fights with Counter Strike up. But a fed Warwick is the real late danger: he flashes or ults past my E, suppresses me through everything, and once I'm low his passive heals off my missing HP and snowballs the duel. I keep the stun for his R channel and Flash for the lock — eat the suppress and it's his fight, dodge the engage and the grind is mine.
edits.after: Past first item the on-hit ramp from Grandmaster's Might plus Trinity out-DPSes his Q heal in a clean side-lane 1v1, so this is where you press the split with Counter Strike up. But a fed Warwick is the real late danger: he flashes or ults past your E, suppresses you for 1.5s on a 70s cooldown, and below 25% Eternal Hunger triples his healing and swings the grind. Keep the stun for his R channel and Flash for the lock — eat the suppress and it is his fight.
